newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: IMF mission to review Philippine progress.
newsitem.headline: IMF mission to review Philippine progress.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) will start consultations with the Philippine government on Friday to review the nation's progress in securing key economic reforms, according to a joint statement from the Central Bank and the IMF.

The review is expected to last for two weeks after which a report will be made to the IMF executive board which will conduct the last review of the three-year Extended Fund Facility programme which is expected to end this at the middle of this year.

"This final review paves the way for the Philippine exit from IMF conditional lending," the statement said."The challenges are to extend the strong track record of accelerating rates of economic growth and declining inflation."

The statement said three major issues still remain which are needed to graduate from the IMF programme. These are the comprehensive tax reform programme, the deregulation of the oil industry and the prompt settlement of obligations to the country's three oil refiners.
Under the IMF's programme for the Philippines, the country is required to meet certain targets, including keeping inflation down and restricting growth of money supply.
The Philippines enacted in November a new tax law on beer and cigarettes but bills restructuring corporate and individual income taxes are still pending in Congress.

The government also has to pay oil companies 2.4 billion pesos ($92 million) in dues from the Oil Price Stablisation Fund (OPSF), a buffer fund meant to help soften the impact of fluctuations in international crude prices.
The Philippines has set February 8 for the full deregulation of the oil industry after adopting an automatic oil pricing formula last August.

Central Bank Governor Gabriel Singson said last month the three issues had to be resolved "if the Philippines is to graduate permanently from the IMF after 35 years and 23 programmes under IMF conditional lending".
